title: POC weekly: onboard ops gate breakdown and bench triage
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on remaining onboarding gates: SSO/KMS integration, gateway credentials, and a discrepant latency regression on p99. SE walked through bench results, suggested batching and small-quant tuning, and outlined a fallback plan to a smaller quantized model for high-throughput endpoints. Security asked for audit log examples and SOC2 doc; Redwood to share. Action items and timeline agreed: infra creds by 8/25, security review docs by 8/24, deep bench run with KV cache on 8/26.
topics: KV cache + batching impact on cost/latency

Customer to deliver staging gateway creds and SSO metadata
SE to re-run bench with KV cache + smaller batch and post results

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel, Jules Park, Marta Ibarra (Redwood); Rina Kapoor, Marco Diaz, Elena Wu, Tom Avery (GreenGrid)
---
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Rina (GreenGrid): hi, Rina here.
[00:08] Marco (GreenGrid): Marco.
[00:10] Elena (GreenGrid): Elena.
[00:11] Tom (GreenGrid): Tom.
[00:12] Jules (Redwood): Jules here.
[00:14] Marta (Redwood): Marta.
[00:16] Samir: Cool. Agenda — gate breakdown, bench triage, security asks, and next steps. Jules will kick off with the perf rundown.
[00:23] Jules (Redwood-SE): ok, quick context. Last week we saw a p99 spike in staging around mid-run; p50/p95 stayed steady but tail blew out to ~680ms which surprised us. We dug into traces: two suspects — KV cache not primed due to short-lived clients, and a small batching config that caused request head-of-line effects. I have the CSVs but I'll summarize.
[00:45] Marco: yeah we saw that on our side too, particularly when we ramped to 150 qps. Our infra team cut the connections faster than the runtime expected.
[00:55] Jules: right, so mitigation on our side is two-fold: enable prefix/KV cache warming and increase the max batch window slightly from 8ms to 12ms for that route. Also try a light quantization profile that keeps fp16 for attention but int8 for linear layers — reduces tokens CPU time without major quality hit.
[01:18] Rina: a few clarifying q's — that quant profile, do we need dedicated infra to run it or is it supported on hosted/dedicated?
[01:25] Jules: supported across hosted and Dedicated. For Dedicated you can pin the quant profile to the worker pool. For hosted we can choose the verified profile that'll live in model catalog; the perf delta is similar but dedicated gives more consistent p99 under sustained load.
[01:40] Tom: what's the expected cost delta if we switch to that profile?
[01:43] Jules: ballpark 8-12% lower per-token cost because kernels are more cache-friendly, but latency variance also drops so fewer retries.
[01:52] Elena (Security): quick interjection — before any dedicated runs we need KMS integration proof, SSO SAML metadata, and sample audit logs. Do you have a SOC2 bundle?
[02:05] Samir: absolutely. We'll send SOC2 + our security pack today. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. We'll share the integration guide and an example request trace with KMS headers redacted.
[02:19] Elena: and the audit logs? Example format?
[02:22] Marta: we can produce a sample of our per-request audit log — it shows request id, model version, timestamp, route, token counts. We'll scrub everything PII.
[02:30] Elena: perfect.
[02:32] Marco: on creds — we still don't have the staging gateway creds. That was the blocker when Jules ran the bench.
[02:38] Samir: noted. Marco, can you share by Wednesday the 25th?
[02:41] Marco: yes we can do 8/25.
[02:44] Samir: great.
[02:46] Jules: back to the bench results — I want to call out an anomaly: during the 10-20 minute window, KV cache hit rate dropped to 12% from 62% because connections cycled. If you can keep client sessions sticky or warm prefixes the hit rate goes back up and p99 falls below 300ms in our tests.
[03:08] Rina: our client side is stateless right now; we planned to spin a small pooling layer. Could you add suggested client-side changes?
[03:15] Jules: yes — we'll send a snippet for pooling/keepalive, and sample TTLs for KV entries. Also note the runtime has an adaptive caching policy; we can tune it for your prompt distribution.
[03:28] Tom: question on fallback — if p99 spikes in production what's the auto fallback?
[03:33] Marta: we support automated routing policies: if latency crosses a threshold we can route to a smaller quantized model or to a different capacity tier (e.g., dedicated hot pool -> fallback to hosted lower-latency variant). We can also do canary rollouts.
[03:50] Marco: what about data residency when routing across regions? We have EU-only data for some customers.
[03:56] Samir: routing honors region and data residency policies — fallback won't cross regulated bounds unless explicitly allowed. We'll show the routing policy examples in the docs.
[04:06] Jules: for the bench rerun I propose: 1) enable KV cache, 2) use pooling to keep connections alive, 3) increase batch window to 12ms for that route, 4) run at target QPS profile (150 peak). I'll run the job and share raw CSV + condensed sheet.
[04:24] Rina: sounds good. How long will the rerun take?
[04:26] Jules: with your prompt set it should be a 30-45 minute job; we'll post results same day.
[04:31] Elena: can you also include token-level cost breakdown? We want to see cost vs latency vs model variant.
[04:36] Jules: yes, I'll include token counts, cache hit rate, and per-route cost estimate.
[04:41] Tom: any privacy concerns with the CSV?
[04:44] Marta: we can anonymize prompts and IDs. We'll only need the prompt patterns, not PII.
[04:49] Marco: looping back to SSO — we started metadata exchange but the SP initiation flow failed in our dev account.
[04:55] Samir: can you paste the error?
[04:57] Marco: it was a 403 on assertion consumer service. Might be mismatch in ACS URL.
[05:02] Samir: ok we'll check. Share the exact assertion and we'll compare. If needed we can do a 1:1 SAML debugging session.
[05:10] Rina: operational question — what are your SLAs for Dedicated? We want to commit if p99 under sustained run meets our threshold.
[05:18] Samir: Dedicated comes with an SLA for availability and latency targets depending on the plan. We can share the SLA matrix; for pilot decision we'll help you pick the smallest reserved pool that meets p99 targets.
[05:28] Tom: competitors — have you seen better tail latency from Anthropic? We saw a bench where their p99 was occasionally lower but cost higher.
[05:36] Jules: it's mixed — some models give lower tails under certain docs but cost profile and model regressions vary. Our aim is reproducible p99 under your workload; that's what the KV/batching adjustments buy you.
[05:49] Elena: ok security follow-up — we'll need the SOC2, a contact for security questionnaire, and sample audit logs.
[05:56] Samir: I'll get that out today.
[05:58] Marta: we'll also attach the routing policy examples and a short write-up on quant profiles.
[06:03] Rina: one more: we saw slight hallucination increase after light quantization in one of your sample profiles — is there a quick QA step?
[06:12] Jules: good catch. We'll run a small quality check on the prompt set as part of the bench and include an eval metric (ROUGE-ish / agreement) against the baseline. That will surface regressions.
[06:23] Tom: timeline check — if we get creds 8/25 and security signoff by 8/24 can you do the bench 8/26 and a deep-dive 8/30?
[06:31] Samir: yes that's doable.
[06:33] Rina: agreed.
[06:35] Samir: quick recap: Marco provide creds 8/25; Elena provide any further security questions; Samir/Marta to send SOC2 + audit samples by EOD 8/22; Jules rerun bench 8/26 with KV/pooling and quant profile; schedule 45m deep-dive week of 8/30. Any final questions?
[06:56] Marco: none.
[06:58] Elena: nope.
[07:00] Jules: thanks all.
[07:02] Samir: thanks folks — we'll follow up with notes and links. End.
---
